# Scope

This document provides a **Methods** section suitable for peer-reviewed papers
that evaluate harvest control rules (HCRs) with a *historical closed-loop
backtest*. The procedure is implemented in the FLR package **FLBacktest**.
Application papers should keep this generic structure and add stock-specific
detail (assessment model, reference-point series, data windows) in separate
subsections or supplementary material.

The backtest separates two questions that are often conflated:

1. whether the assessment and advice rule are robust under historical
   uncertainty; and
2. whether realised management outcomes differ because advice was not followed.

# Overview of the backtest

For each operating-model stock and each advice year $t$ in a predefined
historical window $[t_0, T]$:

1. **Perceive.** Form a management-procedure (MP) view of stock status using
   only information that would have been available at $t$ (perfect
   information, short-cut assessment error, or a full re-assessment / peel).
2. **Advise.** Apply the HCR in force at $t$, with that year's reference
   points, to obtain catch (or $F$) advice for year $t{+}1$.
3. **Implement.** Project the operating model forward under the advised
   control, optionally with implementation error.
4. **Compare.** Contrast the simulated trajectory of spawning-stock biomass
   (SSB), fishing mortality ($F$), and catch with the realised historical
   path over the same years.

Repeating steps 1–3 for successive $t$ builds a counterfactual path under
consistent adherence to advice as it was understood at the time
[@Punt2016MSE; @Butterworth2014].

# Operating model

The operating model (OM) is an age-structured `FLStock` conditioned on a
historical assessment (or a set of plausible assessments). Biological
quantities (weights, maturity, natural mortality, selectivity) follow the
assessment. A stock–recruitment relationship is fitted and represented as an
`FLBRP` equilibrium for short-term forecasts and closed-loop projections
[@Kell2007FLR].

Where robustness is required, multiple OMs may be retained (e.g. alternative
natural mortality or productivity hypotheses). Stochastic recruitment is
represented by multiplicative deviations on the stock–recruit scale; papers
should state whether deviations are treated as aleatory (stationary process)
or include epistemic trend components.

# Observation and estimation error

Three nested observation models are available. Papers should state which are
used as base case and sensitivity runs.

## Perfect information

The MP observes true OM SSB (or the metric used by the HCR) without error.
This isolates HCR behaviour and implementation from assessment error and is a
useful diagnostic, not a realistic advice process.

## Short-cut assessment error

Assessment error is imposed as a multiplicative process on SSB (or another
HCR metric), typically conditioned on retrospective peels
(`now`/`then` ratios). An ARIMA (or AR(1)) model is fitted to the
retrospective bias series and simulated across years and iterations
[@ICES2013EqSim; @Kell2016]. Short-cut backtests avoid re-fitting a full
assessment each year while retaining empirically motivated error magnitude
and autocorrelation.

## Full feedback (assessment-based MP)

Each year the MP re-fits (or updates) an assessment using contemporaneous
catch and survey data generated from the OM, then applies the HCR to the
assessment estimates. Survey indices may be constructed as noisy observations
of abundance. This full feedback loop is computationally heavier but includes
observation, estimation, and advice error jointly [@Punt2016MSE].

# Harvest control rule

The base HCR is the ICES Category 1 MSY hockey-stick (Figure 1 conceptually):

$$
F_{\mathrm{advice}}(B) =
\begin{cases}
0, & B \le B_{\lim}, \\[4pt]
F_{\min} + (F_{\mathrm{tar}} - F_{\min})\,
\dfrac{B - B_{\min}}{B_{\mathrm{trig}} - B_{\min}},
& B_{\lim} < B < B_{\mathrm{trig}}, \\[4pt]
F_{\mathrm{tar}}, & B \ge B_{\mathrm{trig}},
\end{cases}
$$

with $F_{\mathrm{tar}} = F_{\mathrm{MSY}}$,
$B_{\mathrm{trig}} = MSYB_{\mathrm{trigger}}$,
and $B_{\lim}$ as published for advice year $t$ [@ICES2021Advice].
Catch advice is obtained by short-term projection of the perceived stock at
$F_{\mathrm{advice}}$. Optional year-to-year TAC stability constraints
(e.g. $\pm 20\%$) may be applied when SSB is above a stated threshold.

Reference points are those used for advice in year $t$. Benchmark years are
treated as structural breaks when $F_{\mathrm{MSY}}$, $B_{\lim}$, or
$MSYB_{\mathrm{trigger}}$ are redefined.

# Closed-loop projection

Given advised catch (or $F$) for year $t{+}1$, the OM is projected with
`FLasher` / FLR forward methods under the chosen recruitment deviations
[@AdamsFLasher]. The loop then advances to $t{+}2$. Management and data lags
(assessment lag, advice lag, interval between assessments) are stated
explicitly for each case study.

Perfect-management counterfactuals set realised catch equal to advised catch
(no TAC overshoot or political override). Implementation error can be added as
a multiplicative process on catch when that hypothesis is of interest.

# Performance metrics

Realised and counterfactual (or OM) histories are compared using a common set
of metrics, typically including:

- **Biological status** — proportion of years (or probability across
  iterations) with SSB below $B_{\lim}$ and below $MSYB_{\mathrm{trigger}}$;
- **Exploitation** — $F$ relative to $F_{\mathrm{MSY}}$;
- **Yield and stability** — mean and cumulative catch, and interannual
  variability (e.g. AAV);
- **Risk trade-offs** — joint summaries of yield versus probability of falling
  below limit reference points [@Punt2016MSE].

Stock-specific tables feed any cross-stock synthesis of where adherence to
advice would have mattered most, versus where assessment revision or
reference-point change dominates outcomes.

# Software and reproducibility

Analyses use the Fisheries Library in R (FLR): `FLCore`, `FLBRP`, `FLasher`,
and `ggplotFL` [@Kell2007FLR]. Closed-loop backtests are run with
**FLBacktest**, principally:

| Method | Role |
|--------|------|
| `hcrICES()` / `backtest()` | Year-by-year HCR feedback |
| `shortcut()` / `retroBias()` | Short-cut error from peels |
| `samIndex*()` / `omIters()` | Full-feedback assessment inputs |
| `hcrParams()` | HCR parameters from reference points |
| `backtestResults()` | Trajectory extraction |

Application repositories should archive conditioned OMs, scenario grids,
random seeds, and session info so that tables and figures can be regenerated
from saved `RData` without re-running the full simulation.

# Supplementary material (shared R Markdown)

Modular supplementary notes ship with the package and should be reused across
papers rather than rewritten:

| Topic | File under `inst/rmd/` |
|-------|------------------------|
| Conditioning | `01_conditioning.Rmd` |
| Observation error | `02_observation_error.Rmd` |
| Management procedure | `03_management_procedure.Rmd` |
| Performance statistics | `04_performance_statistics.Rmd` |

Locate installed paths with `backtestMaterials()`. Application papers add only
case-study checklists (assessment, window, OEM base case, paper-specific
metrics).

# Case-study subsections (for application papers)

Replace this heading with stock-specific methods, for example:

- Assessment model and peel design (software, data cuts, validation against
  published advice-year assessments);
- Historical window $[t_0, T]$, lags, and TAC constraints;
- Source and time series of reference points;
- OM conditioning choices (natural mortality, SR hypotheses, recruitment
  regimes);
- Which observation model (perfect / short-cut / full) is the base case.
